observationsNotFailures: Round 3 takes the nil-origin rule out of observeAskBlocksForUpdate and leaves it in creditContentChange alone (websocket.go). The two rules are not the same: creditContentChange decides who a content change is credited to, and the ask walk decides who an ask block newly seen on an update is attributed to. After this round, an ask block first seen on ygo's own cleanup transaction would be attributed to the sole connected browser rather than to nobody. I could not construct a reachable case - a cleanup transaction deletes redundant format markers and adds no block, so it cannot make an ask id newly visible, and in every path I tried the ask was already recorded by the update before it - so this is an observation, not a failure. It is recorded because nothing now pins it.
The replay's margin-publish change is the only production change of round 3 on a measured path, and the pairs above cover it: both pairs ran at 073590ff.
